summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/5)

data.turoyo: Mən‿našifiwa, g̥̊ḥurkíwaynanne bu+ḥurako, ŭ ṭowo dhowənwa, ŭ layšiwa, maḥtiwa haqqa d̥qamḥo da+sʕore baynaṯṯe, ŭ saymíwayle laḥmo (laḥmo latwa, qamḥo latwa!).
data.translation: When they dried, we ground them with a grinding stone, and so they became fine [flour], and they kneaded it, put so much barley flour in them, and made bread with it (there wasn’t any bread, there wasn’t any flour!).

rationale: Fills I.1 Infectum-wa from one to two examples, with a distinct acorn-processing passage and an overt bu+ḥurako instrument. It documents a foodstuff patient and the flour result without duplicating the existing herb passage.

summary: Both occurrences have a 1pl agent and -nne plural object in Infectum-wa, supporting repeated past processing procedures. Instruments are expressed with b-: bu+ḥurako in both and additionally bi+manduriye in Interview 2/144.
The source spelling g̥̊ḥurkíwaynanne and its diacritics are preserved. No independent claim about the phonetic value of the marked prefix is made without audio verification.

The supplied entry contains one existing example in Infectum-wa, with its source reference embedded in that example. There is no second independent example to delete. The raw heading ‘Infectum - wa’ is inherited formatting; the existing normalized label and new output use Infectum-wa.
No idiom, new numbered sense, Detransitive use or additional stem is established by these two process descriptions.

The ground patient can be dried acorn pieces, as well as the plants in the inherited example. The same ḥurako-instrument grinding process yields flour in the food passage and paste in the vessel-making passage; this is a participant/material extension, not a new sense.
